finding: The round-12 repair's role clause has nothing to run against and does not cover `cr record`. §6.1.3 now says "`cr merge` MUST reject one whose `role` is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in", but §4.6.2 requires only that "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to" — no file in §2.2 or §2.3 stores that role-to-path assignment (`meta.json` holds "active roles", not their output paths), and `cr merge <files...>` accepts whatever paths the caller passes, so `cr` cannot establish which role an input file belongs to. Meanwhile `cr record <pr> <file>` applies no role check at all — not even the "inactive role" rejection §4.5.6 already requires for cells — and no MUST anywhere binds its input to `cr merge` output; §11 calls it "a round's merged findings" in prose only, and §9.1's transition table lets `cr record` create records directly. Since `axis` is "The axis of the record's `role`, written by `cr`", an unvalidated agent string decides the axis, and §6.2's `cited` bar "the record's `axis` is not `test`" — which carries the whole of §4.4.2's "A test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment" — is bought by stamping `role: correctness` on a test-adequacy record and handing it straight to `cr record`. The same bypass skips §6.4.4's waiver drop and §9.3.6's posted-index drop, both of which fire "at merge".
suggestion: In §6.1.3 replace the merge-only clause with one both commands can execute: "Both MUST also reject a record whose `role` is not an active role of the current round per §4.5.1." Retain a file-correspondence check only if §4.6.2 is also amended to persist the emitted role-to-path assignment in per-PR state.

finding: The `cited` boundary is still agent-selectable, so the unit-swap forgery survives the repair. §6.1.3 now rejects "a record whose `unit` is not a unit of the current round" — that establishes the unit exists, not that it is the record's own. Nothing binds `anchor` to `unit`: §6.1.2 requires only that the anchor "resolves", and no clause requires `anchor.path` to be one of the unit's file paths or `anchor.line` to fall within its hunks. Both fields are agent-written. A record whose defect sits in unit `u1` may therefore declare `unit: u2` — a genuine unit of the same round — and cite a `path:line` inside its own anchored hunk; §6.2's test "lies outside the record's own unit" is then evaluated against u2's hunk ranges, the self-citation passes, and a record with no evidence beyond its own diff reaches the assertion register. §6.2.1's "no field the agent writes can move a location across the boundary" is consequently still false as written: `unit` is the boundary, and the agent picks it.
suggestion: Add to §6.1.3: "Both MUST also reject a record whose `anchor` does not lie inside its `unit` — `anchor.path` among that unit's file paths and `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` within one of its hunk ranges on the unit's side."

finding: The round-13 repair adds a check `cr merge` cannot perform. §6.1 item 3 now says "`cr merge` MUST reject one whose `role` is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in", but nothing binds an input file to a role. §6.5.1 and §11 give merge only positional paths — `cr merge <files...> -o <out> --repo <owner/repo> --pr <number>` — §4.6.2 says only "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to" without fixing a name template, and §2.3's per-PR state table records no fan-out output paths, so the emitted path→role association exists only in the prompt text and is gone by merge time. §4.6.1 further emits "one prompt" per (role, unit), leaving it open whether one file per role or one per cell arrives. An implementer must therefore either invent a filename convention or skip the check, and skipping it reopens exactly the forgery this repair closed: a forged `role` sets the computed `axis` of §6.1, and §6.2's `cited` row turns on `axis` not being `test`.
suggestion: Pin the binding in §4.6.2 by naming the file, e.g. append: "The path MUST end in `<role-id>.ndjson`, so `cr merge` can recover the role from the file name."

finding: The round-13 repair adds an unassertable half. §6.1.3 now says `cr merge` "MUST reject one whose `role` is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in", but nothing binds a file to a role. §4.6.2 says only "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to" — it fixes no path form — and that path is never persisted: §2.3's per-PR state has no entry for it, and §4.6.3 says `cr review` "MUST report the set of cells it expects to be filled", i.e. reports, not stores. `cr merge <files...>` therefore receives bare paths with no recoverable role, so as a test author I cannot construct an input that MUST be accepted or one that MUST be rejected. Two conforming implementations disagree on the same input: (A) `cr review` emits `review-<role>.ndjson` and merge parses the role from the basename, so a file named `out.ndjson` holding one valid `role: correctness` record exits 1; (B) merge takes the file's role from its first record and rejects only later divergent lines, so the same file exits 0. The prompt-level wrinkle compounds it: §4.6.1 emits one prompt per (role, unit) while §6.5.1 merges "per-role NDJSON files", so it is also undetermined whether a role has one output file or one per unit. The sibling `unit` check in the same sentence is fully testable — membership in the current round's `units.ndjson`, and it holds for a LEFT-anchored record too, since §3.4.4 partitions units by side and a LEFT unit id is an ordinary entry there.
suggestion: Fix the path in §4.6.2 so the binding is mechanical: after "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to", add "The path MUST be `review-<role-id>.ndjson`, one file per role." Then narrow §6.1.3's clause to "and `cr merge` MUST reject a record whose `role` is not the `<role-id>` in its input file's basename, and MUST reject with exit code 1 an input file whose basename does not have that form".

finding: §6.1.3's new clause — "`cr merge` MUST reject one whose `role` is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in" — has nothing to resolve a file against a role. §4.6.2 only says "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to"; it never fixes what that path is, and no file in §2.2 or §2.3 records the paths `cr review` emitted, so the emitted path→role association is not durable state. `cr merge <files...> -o <out> --repo <owner/repo> --pr <n>` receives bare paths with no role argument. To build the check I would have to invent one of three different rules: (a) a filename convention such as `review-<role>.ndjson` and parse the basename, (b) a new state file written by `cr review` recording each emitted path, or (c) infer the role from the first record in each file and require the rest to agree — which catches only intra-file mixing and not a whole file written under another role's id, the case that skews §6.4.2's representative selection and §4.5.6's role attribution. §4.6.1 also emits one prompt per (role, unit), so it is not even settled whether a role has one output file or one per unit. The sibling clause in the same sentence, the `unit` check, is buildable — units are round-scoped per §3.4.6, carry `round` and `head` per §2.3.3, live in `units.ndjson`, and `cr merge` reaches them through `--repo`/`--pr`; LEFT-anchored records admitted by §6.1.2 have LEFT units because §3.4.4 partitions by side. Neither clause collides with §6.5.1: `role` and `unit` are agent-written required fields, not computed ones, so rejecting them adds no computed field to merge output.
suggestion: In §4.6.2, fix the path so the role is derivable from it: after "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to", add "which MUST be `review-<role-id>.ndjson`, so §6.1.3 can read the expected role from the basename". Alternatively delete the `role` clause from §6.1.3 and keep only the `unit` check.

finding: Edit 1 added to §6.1.3: "`cr merge` MUST reject one whose `role` is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in", but nothing in the spec lets `cr merge` attribute an input file to a role. §4.6.2 says only "Every prompt MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to" — it does not fix the path's form, does not require the role-to-path map to be persisted (§2.3 lists no such file), and §11's signature `cr merge <files...> -o <out> --repo <owner/repo> --pr <n>` takes arbitrary positional paths with no `--role`. For an input file that is not at a path `cr review` emitted (renamed, copied, or produced out of band), the clause has no referent, and the two natural readings diverge in opposite directions: reject the file, or skip the check. Skipping it re-opens exactly the forgery the edit exists to close — a test-axis role writing `role: correctness` so the computed `axis` escapes §6.2's "the record's `axis` is not `test`" bar.
suggestion: In §4.6.2, after "MUST name the NDJSON path the role writes to", add: "The path MUST be derived from the role id, and `cr merge` MUST reject with exit code 1 an input file that is not one of the current round's paths."

finding: Edit 2 added "the mapping of §4.1.6" to §6.2.1's input list, making the grade depend for the first time on state that is mutable within a round: §4.1.6 lets `cr map record` "replace `mapping.ndjson` for the current round" at any time, and §3.3.1 clears it on every `cr claims record`. Every other input is fixed once the record exists — `axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `claim`, `citations` are record fields, probe records are "immutable once written" (§5.5.1), and units change only on a new head. But §6.3.1 requires the grade to be re-evaluated "at record time, again at draft time, and again at post time", and §7.2.2 requires `cr post` to "recompute every record's grade". So a gap-probe-backed record that graded `argued` at record time — because §5.4.4 found its `claim` unmapped — can be raised to `probed` by a later `cr map record`, and §7.2's marker table then accepts a `question`→`finding` edit "only when the recomputed grade is `probed` or `cited`". The three-time forcing of §6.3.1 presumes recomputation only tightens; the new input lets it loosen after the human has read the draft.
suggestion: In §6.2.1, after "`evidence` prose is never parsed", add: "A recomputed grade MUST NOT be higher than the grade computed at record time."
